title: Precious metals plunge in Indian markets on global cues, strong currencies - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
In the global market, gold and silver prices slid to $3,475 and $39.33 an ounce respectively.

Indian silver prices crashed by ₹10,000 a kg to below ₹1.5 lakh on Wednesday, while gold prices plunged by ₹4,000 per 10 g on cues from the global market and strong currencies.

With silver prices diving below $40 an ounce and gold testing $3,500 an ounce in the global market, domestic prices of the white precious metal closed at ₹1,42,945 a kg, while the yellow precious metal ended at ₹1,21,038. On Tuesday, the closing prices of silver and gold were ₹1,52,625 and ₹1,24,945 respectively.

In the futures market, silver for March delivery ruled at ₹1,44,900 a kg, and gold for February delivery was ₹1,22,505 per 10 g at 1900 hrs IST. Silver had declined by over 20 per cent and gold by 12 per cent so far this month.

In the global market, gold and silver prices slid to $3,475 and $39.33 an ounce respectively. Year-to-date, gold has declined by 19 per cent and silver by 44 per cent, but the fall is steeper from the peak witnessed on January 29 this year.

Bullion prices pared their gains made on Monday as US consumer confidence looked better than initially expected, while sell-offs in technology stocks globally put pressure on precious metals, said analysts. The market is also factoring in a 98 per cent chance of the US Fed hiking interest rates in its December meeting.

“Strength in the dollar and rupee has added to the pressure on domestic bullion prices, while the international market continues to face selling pressure,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.

Gold and silver gave back everything they had gained over the past two sessions, as investors held off ahead of Wednesday’s US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve’s policy path, said Renisha Chainani, Chief Research Officer at Augmont.

The outlook looks gloomy for bullion metals going by the current trend. According to Prithiviraj Kothari, Managing Director at RiddhiSiddhi Bullion Ltd and President of Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association, technically, with gold’s key support at $3,515 broken, it could now head to $3,350 (₹1,14,000/10 g), while silver risks a slide to $37 (₹1,30,000/kg) as $40 psychological support has given way.

Darshan Desai, CEO of Aspect Bullion & Refinery, said the recent price correction has brought some buyers back into the market, particularly with the wedding season supporting demand.

“However, purchases remain selective, with consumers closely tracking price movements and looking for favourable buying levels,” he said, adding that going forward, demand is likely to be shaped by price stability, global cues and domestic consumer sentiment.

Gold and silver surged to a record highs of $5,608 and $121.62 an ounce on January 29 this year, but the Iran war has lead to the precious metal shedding their gains due to a stronger dollar, higher Treasury yields and hopes of higher US Fed rates due to surging inflation. Higher crude oil prices have also played a role.

Precious metals had a splendid run from 2024 to January 2026 on hopes of US Fed rate cuts, geopolitical tensions and the trade war between the US and its other global partners.
